JobState.description: A job's lifecycle state on the wire.

oneOf.description: Enqueued, awaiting a dispatcher to claim it.

Enqueued, but intentionally held back: the run's harness is already at its
configured maximum parallelism, so the backend will not hand it to a
dispatcher until an in-flight run of the same harness finishes; or the whole
queue is on hold because the artifact store cannot take another run's tree.
Distinct from `queued` (which is free to be claimed the moment a dispatcher
has capacity) so an operator can see a run is deliberately waiting rather
than merely next in line.
Claimed by the dispatcher; the driver Job is being created.

The driver pod is up and running the pre-run setup (connecting to the
container runtime, materializing the definition) — not yet executing the
harness, but it will as soon as setup finishes.
The driver is executing the run's harness session: the model is working.

The harness session has ended and the driver is doing the post-session work
(collecting the tree, the post-run analysis, the case's toolchain, validation
and the upload of the tree). Still in flight and driven exactly like
`running`.

The run has finished and its driver is waiting to store its artifact tree,
because the artifact store could not take it. The driver holds the only copy
and keeps retrying. While any job is in this state the backend hands out no
new run.
The run could not be driven to a record.
The job was canceled before completing.

description: A job's status, as `GET /jobs/{id}` reports it.

detail.description:
A human-readable reason: why the job failed or was canceled, or why its
driver is waiting while `state` is `storing`.

recordId.description:
The produced run record's id, present once `state` is `succeeded` and the
run was completed (the row the console navigates to).

state.description: Where the job is in its lifecycle.
